decisions.reason: Memory-clock has the lowest trajectory-level CV error (0.00163), far below the state model; PRBS maximizes disagreement among plausible history models.
decisions.prediction: After PRBS input returns to zero, the response will retain input-history dependence, with any periodic component aligned to elapsed time.

mapping.target_relation: Accumulated input history predicts a response after current input is controlled, consistent with finite-leakage storage.
mapping.condition_to_check: Compare post-input responses across PRBS histories at matched elapsed times; absent history dependence would contradict this relation.

decisions.reason: Memory_slow has the best trajectory-level CV error (0.00390), outperforming memory_clock (0.00727); persistent post-input responses support history dependence, while residual correlation cautions that the model may remain incomplete.
decisions.prediction: After alternating input ends, the response will retain history dependence and decay without a persistent elapsed-time periodic component.

mapping.target_relation: Past input predicts post-input response, consistent with finite-leakage storage.
mapping.condition_to_check: Compare responses after distinct alternating histories at matched elapsed times; no history dependence would contradict this relation.

decisions.reason: Memory_multiscale has the lowest trajectory-level CV NMSE (0.001345), slightly below memory_clock and saturating_memory. Residual lag correlation and failed prior model selections leave adequacy uncertain.
decisions.prediction: After the slow wave ends, the response will decay with history-dependent contributions on multiple timescales, not persist as an elapsed-time oscillation.

mapping.target_relation: Post-input responses depend on past inputs, consistent with accumulated history having finite leakage.
mapping.condition_to_check: Compare post-wave decay after distinct histories at matched elapsed times; absent history dependence would contradict this relation.
